dataset.description: A non-targeted metabolomics study of semi-polar compounds in plasma was performed in rabbits from the homogenous (HO) and heterogenous (HE) lines in litter size. A liquid chromatograph (Thermo Scientific Vanquish) coupled to a high resolution quadrupole-orbitrap mass spectrometer (Q Exactive™ HF Hybrid Quadrupole-Orbitrap, Thermo Fisher Scientific) was used. The analysis was performed in positive and negative ionisation modes. Thermo Scientific Compound Discoverer 3.3 was used to extract the peak areas.

dataset.description: A selection experiment is being carried out to decrease and increase the environmental variance of litter size at birth in rabbits (the homogeneous and the heterogeneous lines) at Miguel Hernández University (UMH). Intra-female variance of litter size, after pre-correction for season-year and parity-lactation order, has been used as a direct measure of environmental variance. It should be noted that this is the first time that it has been selected directly on the  environmental variance, treating it as an observed character. Environmental variance is directly related to resilience.

dmp.description:
About DMP
The DMP will guide all data collection, processing, production, and storage of the Proyectos I+D+i 2021 RABBIT-RESILIENS project (Grant No. PID2021-123702OB-I00). The DMP in ARGOS describes all datasets that will be created, managed, and curated in the context of the project. All datasets will be stored in the Digital Repository of the Miguel Hernández University (https://hdl.handle.net/11000/33915) and linked to the DMP in ARGOS.

About the project
The aim of this project is to investigate the biological, metabolomic and genetic mechanisms controlling resilience, i.e. resistance response to stress and disease, in order to create a new maternal line for the rabbit industry. A selection experiment to decrease and increase environmental variance in litter size at birth in rabbits (the homogeneous line and the heterogeneous line) is being carried out at the Miguel Hernández University (UMH) that will be continued until generation 18. It should be noted that this is the first time that environmental variance is selected directly, treating it as an observed trait. Our team has proposed the environmental variance in litter size as a criterion to select for resilience. In this project, a comparative study of stress sensitivity between the homogenous line (HO) and the heterogeneous line (HE) will be carried out. For this purpose, blood levels of the corticotropin-releasing factor (CRF), the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and the glucocorticoids will be measured in animals from generation 13. In addition, in these animals, a non-targeted metabolomics study will be performed in plasma to identify metabolites related to the differences in resilience found between the HO and the HE lines. Identifying differences in metabolites between the lines may help us to understand the mechanisms and metabolic pathways that regulate resilience. In the 17th generation of the UMH experiment, a validation study of the main variants (SNPs) of the candidate genes found in the 12th generation related to response to stress and diseases will be carried out. The Open Array platform will be used for this.
